newsitem.title: USA: Energy funding clears Senate, goes to White House.
newsitem.headline: Energy funding clears Senate, goes to White House.

text.p: The Senate Tuesday approved a $20 billion bill funding the Energy Department and federal water programmes for the 1997 fiscal year and sent the measure to President Clinton for his signature.

The House-Senate compromise measure passed the Senate 92-8 after clearing the House 383-29 last week. It provides $465 million more than in 1996, but about $200 million less than the president requested. However, he is expected to accept it.

Administration officials said the bill was acceptable. "We think that generally the committee has done a very fine job and we support the bill," said Deputy Energy Secretary Charles Curtis before the House vote last week.
Half the funding was devoted to the Energy Department's nuclear weapons activities and nuclear waste cleanup.

A large portion, $1.1 billion, funds Army Corps of Engineers projects, a boost of $277 million above 1996. It also includes $9 milion to build the controversial Animas-La Plata water project in Colorado.
Washington will pay more than half the final expected cost of $700 million to complete the project.

The Energy budget included $3.9 billion for nuclear weapons management -- weapons storage and scientific testing -- and $5.45 billion for cleanup of radioactive waste left from 50 years of weapons manufacturing.
